## About this document

This document records every step from the raw metadata files in `data/raw/` to one harmonised metadata table in `data/processed/`. Nothing is edited by hand: to change a result, change the code and render again.

The data are synthetic and were created for this workshop. They mimic gut microbiome studies at three South African sites (Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban).

This is the completed version of the participant template.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(here)       # file paths relative to the project root
library(readr)      # reading text files
library(dplyr)      # data manipulation
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)    # text cleaning
library(lubridate)  # dates
library(janitor)    # clean_names(), convert_to_date()

# Every way the sites wrote "missing"
na_codes <- c("", "NA", "N/A", "-", "missing", "999", "unknown")
```

## 1. Read the raw data

Everything is read as text first, so that nothing is silently converted or lost. Each file has its own quirks.

```{r}
#| label: read-raw
site_a_raw <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "siteA_capetown_metadata.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)

# Site B uses semicolons as separators and decimal commas
site_b_raw <- read_delim(
  here("data", "raw", "siteB_johannesburg_metadata.csv"),
  delim = ";", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)

# Site C is tab-separated and has a second header row holding the units
site_c_raw <- read_tsv(
  here("data", "raw", "siteC_durban_metadata.tsv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
) |>
  slice(-1)  # drop the units row (record the units in the data dictionary instead)

glimpse(site_a_raw)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Look before you clean
Use `View(site_a_raw)`, `count(site_a_raw, Sex)` and `distinct(site_a_raw, Storage temp)` (with backticks around names containing spaces) in the console to find the problems. Make a list of what needs fixing before writing any cleaning code.
:::

## 2. Site A (Cape Town): worked example

```{r}
#| label: clean-site-a
site_a <- site_a_raw |>
  clean_names() |>                                       # "Sample ID" -> sample_id
  mutate(across(everything(), str_trim)) |>              # remove stray spaces
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x %in% na_codes, NA_character_, .x))) |>
  distinct() |>                                          # remove exact duplicate rows
  mutate(
    samp_name            = str_to_upper(str_remove_all(sample_id, "[-_ ]")),
    host_subject_id      = participant,
    site                 = "Cape Town",
    geo_loc_name         = "South Africa:Western Cape",
    host_age             = parse_number(age),
    host_sex             = case_when(
      str_to_lower(sex) %in% c("f", "female") ~ "female",
      str_to_lower(sex) %in% c("m", "male")   ~ "male"
    ),
    host_body_mass_index = parse_number(str_replace(bmi, ",", ".")),
    collection_date      = as_date(parse_date_time(collection_date, orders = c("Ymd", "dmY", "dbY"))),
    samp_store_temp      = parse_number(str_replace(storage_temp, "minus ", "-")),
    notes                = notes
  )

count(site_a, host_sex)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## One value needs a decision
One participant at Site A has an age of 340. Do not guess the correct value in the data. Decide what to do (for example, query the site and set it to missing until confirmed), do it in code, and write the decision in `data/README.md`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: site-a-age-decision
# Age 340 was queried with Site A; set to missing until the site confirms the value
site_a <- site_a |> mutate(host_age = if_else(host_age > 110, NA_real_, host_age))
```

## 3. Site B (Johannesburg): your turn

Check `data/raw/siteB_codebook.txt` first.

```{r}
#| label: clean-site-b
site_b <- site_b_raw |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(across(everything(), str_trim)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x %in% na_codes, NA_character_, .x))) |>
  mutate(
    samp_name            = str_to_upper(str_remove_all(sample, "[-_ ]")),
    host_subject_id      = subject_id,
    site                 = "Johannesburg",
    geo_loc_name         = "South Africa:Gauteng",
    host_age             = as.numeric(age_years),
    host_sex             = case_when(gender == "1" ~ "male", gender == "2" ~ "female"),
    host_body_mass_index = as.numeric(str_replace(bmi_kg_m2, ",", ".")),
    collection_date      = convert_to_date(date_collected),  # handles Excel serials and the one typed date
    samp_store_temp      = parse_number(freezer_temp_c),
    notes                = NA_character_
  )
```

## 4. Site C (Durban): your turn

```{r}
#| label: clean-site-c
site_c <- site_c_raw |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(across(everything(), str_trim)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x %in% na_codes, NA_character_, .x))) |>
  mutate(
    samp_name            = str_to_upper(sample_name),
    host_subject_id      = host_id,
    site                 = "Durban",
    geo_loc_name         = "South Africa:KwaZulu-Natal",
    host_age             = floor(as.numeric(age) / 12),       # months to completed years
    host_sex             = case_when(
      str_to_lower(host_sex) %in% c("f", "female") ~ "female",
      str_to_lower(host_sex) %in% c("m", "male")   ~ "male"
    ),
    host_body_mass_index = parse_number(body_mass_index),
    collection_date      = as_date(ymd_hm(collection_datetime)),
    samp_store_temp      = parse_number(storage),
    notes                = comments
  )
```

## 5. Combine and apply the standard

```{r}
#| label: harmonise
mixs_columns <- c("samp_name", "host_subject_id", "site", "geo_loc_name",
                  "collection_date", "host_age", "host_sex",
                  "host_body_mass_index", "env_medium", "samp_store_temp", "notes")

harmonised <- bind_rows(site_a, site_b, site_c) |>
  mutate(
    env_medium           = "feces [UBERON:0001988]",       # same material at all sites
    host_body_mass_index = round(host_body_mass_index, 1)  # same precision at all sites
  ) |>
  select(all_of(mixs_columns)) |>
  arrange(samp_name)

head(harmonised)
```

## 6. Check the result

Write checks as code, so they run every time the data change.

```{r}
#| label: validate
validation <- tibble(
  check = c("Duplicate sample names",
            "Age outside 18 to 110",
            "Sex not female/male (or missing)",
            "Collection date outside 2025",
            "Stored warmer than -70 °C"),
  n_problems = c(
    sum(duplicated(harmonised$samp_name)),
    sum(!between(harmonised$host_age, 18, 110), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(!harmonised$host_sex %in% c("female", "male", NA)),
    sum(year(harmonised$collection_date) != 2025, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(harmonised$samp_store_temp > -70, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
validation

# Missing values per column
harmonised |> summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing")
```

```{r}
#| label: flagged-samples
# Samples a reviewer should know about
harmonised |> filter(samp_store_temp > -70 | !is.na(notes)) |> select(samp_name, samp_store_temp, notes)
```

## 7. Merge with the sequencing run sheet

The sequencing facility used its own library names (e.g. `CT001_S12`), and the run includes negative controls and a mock community.

```{r}
#| label: merge-sequencing
seq_runs <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "sequencing_run_sheet.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    samp_name   = str_remove(Library_ID, "_S[0-9]+$"),
    sample_type = if_else(str_detect(samp_name, "^(NEG|NTC|MOCK)"), "control", "sample")
  )

# Samples with metadata but no sequencing data
anti_join(harmonised, seq_runs, by = "samp_name") |> select(samp_name, site)

# Sequenced libraries with no metadata (should only be controls)
anti_join(seq_runs, harmonised, by = "samp_name") |> select(Library_ID, sample_type)

samples_sequenced <- left_join(harmonised, seq_runs, by = "samp_name")
```

## 8. Save

```{r}
#| label: save
dir.create(here("data", "processed"), showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(harmonised, here("data", "processed", "metadata_harmonised.csv"), na = "not provided")
write_csv(samples_sequenced, here("data", "processed", "metadata_with_sequencing.csv"), na = "not provided")
```

## 9. Methods (writing exercise)

Inline code fills in the versions automatically, so this text is always true for the run that produced it.

> Sample metadata from three sites were harmonised in R (`r R.version.string`) using readr (v`r packageVersion("readr")`), dplyr (v`r packageVersion("dplyr")`), stringr (v`r packageVersion("stringr")`), lubridate (v`r packageVersion("lubridate")`) and janitor (v`r packageVersion("janitor")`). Variable names and formats followed the MIxS standard (human-associated fields). Missing values were recorded as "not provided". Site C ages, recorded in months, were converted to completed years. One implausible age (340 years) was set to missing pending confirmation from the site. Body mass index values recorded with decimal commas were converted to decimal points, and dates recorded in several formats (including Excel serial numbers) were converted to ISO 8601. In total, `r nrow(harmonised)` samples from `r n_distinct(harmonised$site)` sites were included.
